title: Father's Shadow
next_chapter_hook: Ye Qing's voice drifted through the night wind, uttering a name that made Chen Ji's body tremble violently—a title he had called out countless times in his midnight dreams, an indelible brand seared into the depths of his bloodline.

text.content: The night wind was biting, causing the tent to flutter violently. Chen Ji stood rooted in place, allowing the residual resonance of the blood pulse to surge within him, yet his gaze locked onto the Demonic Path Saint before him like a hawk's. There was something in her expression that he couldn't see through—not hostility, nor complete goodwill, but something far more complex.

dialogue.content: "That aura you carry..." Ye Qing suddenly spoke, her voice several degrees lower than before, "bears a striking resemblance to a portrait I've seen in the Sacred Canon. That was the last legitimate inheritor of the Tianji Record, three hundred years ago."

text.content: Chen Ji's heart skipped a beat. Three hundred years ago—this timespan far exceeded his expectations. He had assumed the secrets of the Tianji Record only involved people and events from the past century, never imagining it stretched so far back. Legitimate inheritor—what did that title mean? What kind of ending had befallen those who held it before him?

dialogue.content: "The person in that portrait..." Chen Ji spoke slowly, his voice so calm it was nearly cold, "did they have any distinguishing features?"

Ye Qing slightly furrowed her brow, as if recalling: "The figure in the painting appeared middle-aged, wearing a blue robe, with a faint golden vertical mark between their brows. The Sacred Canon records that they were called the 'Son of Heavenly Mandate,' said to possess the ability to peer into Heavenly Secrets, and ultimately... vanished mysteriously."

text.content: Blue robe. Vertical brow mark. Chen Ji's breath caught abruptly. These features— they matched perfectly with the name he'd heard since childhood. His father Chen Tianming, the last time he appeared before the family before disappearing, had been wearing that faded blue robe. And his mother's dying murmur—"The mark on his brow began to glow"—now exploded in his mind like thunder.

However, he revealed no trace of abnormality on his face. Years of restraint had long taught him how to hide tumultuous waves beneath the stillness of dead water. He merely gently lowered his eyelashes and asked in the most ordinary tone: "Did that 'Son of Heavenly Mandate'... leave a name behind?"

dialogue.content: Ye Qing shook her head: "The Sacred Canon only records his title. But there is a detail—" she paused, as if choosing her words carefully, "It's said his inheritance wasn't obtained through proper channels, but self-comprehended from a fragment. That fragment... seems somehow connected to the one in your hands."

text.content: Chen Ji felt the Tianji Record in his chest grow warm. This reaction was all too familiar to him— whenever significant clues surfaced, the fragment would remind him in this manner. Yet at this moment, that heat felt like a branding iron, searing his heart with pain. Father... could he truly have been the previous master of the Tianji Record? Then his disappearance—

dialogue.content: There's something else I've heard." Chen Ji suddenly lifted his gaze, a barely perceptible cold light flickering in his eyes, "It's said that 'Son of Heavenly Mandate' didn't simply vanish, but was... erased by the Eyes of Heavenly Dao.

Ye Qing's form visibly stiffened for an instant. She hadn't expected this seemingly废物-like servant disciple to know the Tianji Record's secrets so deeply. After a moment, she nodded: "Indeed. The annotations in the Sacred Canon do mention that the 'Son of Heavenly Mandate' attempted to peer into forbidden knowledge and was struck down by divine punishment from the Eyes of Heavenly Dao, leaving no remains.

text.content: No remains. Chen Ji冷笑 in his heart. What a convenient 'no remains.' He still remembered the scene the night his father disappeared—moonlight like water, his father standing in the courtyard gazing at the starry sky, the vertical mark between his brows that was usually hidden now faintly glowing with golden light. As a child he hadn't understood what that meant, but looking back now, that was clearly—the awakening of Heavenly Mandate power.

Eyes of Heavenly Dao..." Chen Ji murmured these four characters, each syllable like a poisoned blade. Mo Xiansheng had told him that the Eyes of Heavenly Dao were beings that transcended everything, regarding all seers throughout history as chess pieces, with the Tianji Record merely one of its pieces spread across the mortal realm. If his father truly was erased for peering into forbidden knowledge—

Then wasn't the fragment in his hands being watched by that invisible eye from the very beginning? Chen Ji's fingertips grew cold. He thought of Mo Xiansheng's expression each time he started to speak but held back, of the Heavenly Fate consumption after each use of the Tianji Record, of those seemingly coincidental yet inevitable disasters— so it was all under the gaze of that eye from the start.

dialogue.content: You..." Ye Qing suddenly sensed something, and her gaze toward Chen Ji gained a more probing quality, "seem to know more than I do?"

text.content: Chen Ji did not answer her question. He slowly raised his head, moonlight falling upon his face, reflecting those ink-black eyes as profoundly unfathomable. He looked at Ye Qing and suddenly asked: "Do you know the true name of that 'Son of Heavenly Mandate'?" He shouldn't have asked this question—asking it meant revealing his connection to the matter. But he needed confirmation—even if only a one-in-ten-thousand possibility.

dialogue.content: Ye Qing was silent for a moment, as if undergoing some internal struggle. Finally, she softly said: "There is a page in the Sacred Canon that records that name. But that page..." her voice dropped, "is sealed by the Holy Lord in the deepest part of the Forbidden Grounds, inaccessible to ordinary people."

text.content: The Holy Lord's Forbidden Grounds. Chen Ji firmly记住了 this information. On the surface, this clue seemed to point toward the Demonic Path Holy Sect, but his intuition told him things were far from that simple. He had been young when his father disappeared, his mother's dying mutterings were fragmented, and the Tianqing Sect Senior Sister Lin Xiao's attitude toward him— could all of this point to the same truth?

Ye Qing watched Chen Ji lost in contemplation, an odd feeling stirring within her. There were too many things about this servant disciple she couldn't see through. When the Eyes of Heavenly Dao had been mentioned just now, his reaction had been too calm, as if he already knew; and now, his gaze was so deep it was like a millennium-old cold pond, making even this Demonic Path Saint who had seen countless schemes and intrigues feel somewhat unnerved.

dialogue.content: Who exactly are you?" These words almost slipped from Ye Qing's lips involuntarily. The moment she said it, she regretted it—this wasn't a question she should ask, nor was this curiosity she should display. But that inexplicable sense of familiarity left her unable to control herself, as if the person before her was bound by some causal connection she was destined to touch.

text.content: Upon hearing this, the corner of Chen Ji's lips lifted in an extremely shallow arc. That smile vanished in an instant, yet carried a chilling implication. He didn't answer Ye Qing's question, but instead turned and said: "The 'Son of Heavenly Mandate' from three hundred years ago—what connection does he have with your Demonic Path Holy Sect? Why would his portrait be recorded in the Sacred Canon?"

dialogue.content: Ye Qing's expression shifted slightly. This question touched upon the Holy Sect's core secrets, and she shouldn't have revealed it. However, for some reason, facing Chen Ji's eyes that were calm to the point of being near lifeless, she felt an illusion that he already knew the answer. This illusion made her back grow cold, forcing her to involuntarily speak: "Because... that 'Son of Heavenly Mandate' personally founded the Demonic Path Holy Sect."

text.content: These words struck like thunder in Chen Ji's mind. The person who founded the Demonic Path Holy Sect was actually a legitimate inheritor of the Tianji Record? Then what relationship existed between the current "Holy Lord" controlling the Holy Sect and his father? Betrayal, inheritance, or— some deeper conspiracy? Chen Ji felt an invisible hand that had been manipulating everything since the moment of his birth.

choice.prompt: The information Ye Qing revealed crashed like waves against Chen Ji's cognition. His father's secrets, the origins of the Tianji Record, the establishment of the Demonic Holy Sect—all of this intertwined, forming a massive chess game he had never imagined. At this moment, he had to make a choice.

choices.description: Find the holy text fragment at all costs to confirm whether that name is indeed his father Chen Tianming
choices.visible_cost: Revealing the connection to the Tianji Record may draw the attention of the Eyes of Heavenly Way
choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial clues about his father's fate
choices.risk_hint: Venturing into the tiger's den, danger is unpredictable

dialogue.content: "I need that page of the fragment." Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet carried unwavering resolve. He gazed at Ye Qing, a sharp glint flickering in his eyes. "Since you've told me all this, you must have a way to let me see it."

text.content: Ye Qing stared into his eyes and suddenly realized this person was by no means some worthless servant disciple. That aura, that composure remaining calm even amidst terrifying waves—these were not things an ordinary person could fake. Somewhere in her heart, something subtly loosened—perhaps cooperating with this person was the right choice.

choices.description: Temporarily suppress the churning emotions within, silently store the clues, and investigate another day
choices.visible_cost: The truth is temporarily buried, but one's cards are preserved
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the worthless persona, arouse no suspicion
choices.risk_hint: Missed a good opportunity, but preserved room for future maneuvering

dialogue.content: "Thank you for the information." Chen Ji slightly nodded, his face donned with that harmless smile once more. "I was merely curious and asking out of habit. After all... for a servant disciple to know these things is already enough."

text.content: Ye Qing stared at him for a moment, then suddenly let out a light laugh. That laughter carried a hint of mockery, but more so a tacit understanding. A worthless servant? If he truly were worthless, how could he remain as steady as a rock after hearing such news? This person's acting truly reached the point of deceiving even the discerning.

The night wind seemed to grow colder. Chen Ji stood there with lowered eyes, beneath the seemingly calm surface, countless thoughts intertwined like vipers. His father from three hundred years ago—no, if his father already existed at that time, what did "three hundred years ago" even mean? Had he miscalculated the timeline, or was there something else hidden within? The origins of the Tianji Record were far more ancient than imagined, and the criteria for selecting inheritors was even more unfathomable.

Chen Ji suddenly remembered what Mo Xiansheng said during their first conversation—"The Tianji Record chose you, and it was not by chance." At the time, he thought it was merely an ordinary remark about inheritance, but looking back now, it tasted entirely different. What were the criteria for the Tianji Record to choose an inheritor? Bloodline? Talent? Or some deeper layer of karma? If his father was truly the previous inheritor, then what was the reason he was "skipped"?

More importantly—did his father even die or not? Chen Ji closed his eyes, and that scene surfaced once more: beneath the moonlight, his father's brow center glowed with golden patterns, then his figure swayed, vanishing like evaporation into the night. His mother wept heartbreakingly, repeatedly murmuring one phrase—"He's gone, he was taken away..." Taken away? By whom? The Eyes of Heavenly Way? Or someone else entirely?

dialogue.content: There's one more thing." Ye Qing suddenly spoke, pulling Chen Ji back to reality from his tangled thoughts. "Before that 'Heavenly Fate Child' disappeared, it's said he left behind a prophecy—'My bloodline shall return after three hundred years, when the Heavenly Secrets reunite and the chess game reaches its end.'

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. After three hundred years—it had been approximately... over twenty years since his father's disappearance. What did this mean? Had he miscalculated the time, or did this prophecy mean something else entirely? Bloodline returning—could it refer to him? No, he was merely a servant disciple who accidentally obtained the fragment. What kind of bloodline connection could exist between him and that "Heavenly Fate Child"?

Yet at this moment, a cold voice rang out in his heart: Was it truly just coincidence? Why did Mo Xiansheng specifically choose him? Why did the Tianji Record awaken when he was at his most desperate? Why did the Eyes of Heavenly Way show him special "attention" from the very beginning? Behind all these coincidences, was there an invisible hand at work?

dialogue.content: Ye Qing watched the changes in Chen Ji's expression and suddenly said softly: "I told you these things because your aura reminds me of that person. But I also want to warn you—" her voice lowered, "the Holy Master's obsession with the Tianji Record far exceeds your imagination. If you truly are that person's... bloodline inheritor, then the Holy Master will never let you go.

text.content: Chen Ji slowly raised his head, his gaze toward Ye Qing carrying a more complex meaning. The Holy Master—the controller of the Demonic Holy Sect, an existence even Ye Qing the Holy Maiden had to handle with utmost care. If this person discovered the connection between him and the "Heavenly Fate Child," what awaited him? He dared not think, nor wished to think. But he knew, from this moment on, everything was different.

dialogue.content: "What are you thinking?" Ye Qing suddenly asked, her gaze directly locking onto Chen Ji's eyes. She had seen too many people's fearful or greedy丑态 after learning such news, but this person... his eyes held no fear, no greed, only a kind of cold, pond-like composure that felt unfamiliar to her.

text.content: Chen Ji did not answer her question. He merely slightly turned his head, gazing toward the night-shrouded horizon in the distance. Moonlight carved a cold, hard outline on his face, making his expression increasingly enigmatic. After a moment, he said softly: "A prophecy from three hundred years ago, a chess game three hundred years later... Who is playing this game?"

This was spoken softly, yet it made Ye Qing's heart jolt. She suddenly realized that the depth of thought behind this servant disciple far exceeded her imagination. His gaze had pierced through three hundred years of mist, gazing toward a more distant future—one that even the Eye of Heaven could not predict.

Chen Ji turned around, casting one final glance at Ye Qing. Beneath the moonlight, his face was tranquil to the point of coldness, yet deep within his eyes, a dark flame slowly burned. It was a burning desire for truth, an unwillingness to accept fate, and an overwhelming hatred toward that existence manipulating everything from the shadows.

"Regardless of whose blood flows through me, and no matter who orchestrates this chess game—" Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet each word rang with crystal clarity. "Anyone who dared to touch my father, I will not let a single one escape." With that, he turned and walked away, his silhouette vanishing into the night. Ye Qing stood frozen in place, gazing at the fading figure, when an absurd notion suddenly struck her: perhaps this person truly had the power to overturn the entire game.
